name: Meridian Coffee Roasters

do: Talk about the farmers and the roast, not just the flavour notes
State dates, timings and weights as plain facts
Name the region and the grower when describing a coffee
Say plainly what a product does not include
Use everyday words for taste, like chocolate, citrus or nutty
dont: Never use wine-tasting vocabulary such as terroir, bouquet, mouthfeel or finish
Never claim a health benefit for coffee
Never call the coffee artisanal, craft, curated or hand-crafted
Never call anything revolutionary, game-changing or disruptive
Never address the reader as a coffee lover, connoisseur or aficionado
Never imply a coffee is rare, exclusive or running out in order to hurry the reader
Never use the words journey, passion or obsession about the roastery

offerings.name: Roaster's Choice Subscription
offerings.description: A rotating 340g bag of our current favourite single-origin, roasted fresh and delivered every four weeks.

offerings.name: Origins Gift Box
offerings.description: A one-time gift box with three 200g bags from three different origins, plus a tasting card.

positioning: For people who check the roast date before the flavour notes, Meridian roasts to order in small batches and ships inside 48 hours — because coffee is perishable, and a supermarket shelf is where it goes to die.

composition_plan.intent: Open on the first row of the spec split: the business name and its plainest promise held in the wide column, a single flat visual field beside it, label in the narrow column. Establishes immediately that this page is a document, not a pitch.
State the problem the business exists to solve at large size, with the narrow column carrying the sober detail behind it. This is where the reader recognises their own cupboard.
Show the sequence from order placed to bag delivered as an ordered list, one line per step, so the timing claim reads as a procedure that can be checked rather than a boast.
Put the offerings side by side, one column each, with matching rows so weight, cadence, price and what is excluded line up and can be compared without reading prose.
A band of the given figures under short labels — founding year, batch and timing facts — flipping the narrow column to the other side so the rule moves down the page.
One full-width row per idea about growers, origins and how the roast is decided, so the human part of the story gets air after the dense comparison rows.
A single quiet band of short attributions that anchors the roastery in a real street and a real trade, without a testimonial carousel.
Answer the shipping, skipping, cancelling and not-included questions where a buyer actually hesitates, so nothing has to be softened elsewhere on the page.
Close with the address, email and phone and nothing else, ending the specification sheet on a physical location.
